summary: This reference maps Hoplight's implemented engine and tool architecture. Hub and spoke explains why every external format maps through one canonical model. The canonical entity defines the shared wrapper and superset rule; escrow preserves source twins and binary carriers without moving private or executable payloads across formats. The adapter contract uses a kind-discriminated open format system, attaches serialization-loss reports, and routes canonical JSON through strict per-kind decoders. defineExhaustiveShape<T>() demands exact schema input and output parity, rejecting drift escapes such as narrowed unions and coercion while leaving declared record bags open. Detection ranks confident kind-correct adapters, and folder discovery supplies the registry. Bundles extract and re-embed lorebook references. Semantic content capabilities define pure previews, progressive discovery, bounded reads and stored results, independently reviewed semantic docs, and explicit compare-and-save apply with re-read verification. Layering points dependencies inward; CLI remains a thin engine surface; source-of-truth links name the governing modules.

sections.title: The one idea: hub and spoke
sections.summary: Every external format maps to and from one canonical superset rather than converting directly to every other format. A pairwise mesh requires N times N minus one paths; hub and spoke needs only N adapters. Adding a format therefore adds one adapter without changing existing formats or core conversion logic. Import calls the adapter's toCanonical operation, export calls fromCanonical, and conversion composes those two steps. This is the architectural invariant behind adapter independence and honest interoperability.

sections.title: The canonical entity
sections.summary: src/core/canonical.ts defines the shared wrapper: schemaVersion identifies the canonical revision, kind selects the entity family, id is the stable identity, body contains interoperable content, profiles hold sparse per-platform overrides, and original holds source escrow. Character, lorebook, persona, preset, regex, and quickreply are adapter-backed kinds; canonical schemas also define pack and htmldoc entities. Body details live in their entity folders rather than in the wrapper. The superset rule limits body fields to meaning represented by at least one real wire format. Values that exist only in one application's memory or have no portable producer remain in escrow instead of acquiring a misleading canonical slot.

children.title: The superset rule
children.summary: Canonical bodies contain only fields serialized by real formats. A field earns a first-class slot only when a wire producer exists. Application-only values, including five RoleCall lorebook fields, stay escrowed so Hoplight does not promise unsupported portability.

sections.title: Escrow: semantic round-trips, contained cross-format loss
sections.summary: Each imported entity keeps an original escrow entry containing the source format, parsed raw twin, and fields not mapped into the canonical body. On same-format export, the adapter clones that twin and re-projects edited canonical fields onto it. Untouched source-specific extensions, layout, identifiers, and scripts survive while edited values are re-encoded. This is a semantic and escrow-preservation guarantee; byte identity applies only where a format specification declares and tests a byte-level tier. Cross-format conversion intentionally carries canonical meaning only. It does not blindly copy private extension blocks, bespoke layout, trigger scripts, or other executable payloads into a different application's file; future extension mapping must be explicit per field. Escrow can also retain sourceMedia with base64 bytes and MIME type. Tavern-lineage PNG adapters use it to preserve the authored portrait carrier for same-format re-emission, while text inputs omit it.

sections.title: The adapter contract
sections.summary: src/core/adapter.ts defines a kind-discriminated union of open format plugins whose character, lorebook, persona, preset, regex, and quickreply branches convert to and from matching canonical entities. Adapter output carries text or bytes, extension, and a SerializeReport naming escrowed, dropped, shadowed, and warning paths. An adapter normally owns the source twin under its own id; escrowFormatIds explicitly declares family-keyed twins when a narrower wire adapter owns one, such as rolecall-preset owning original.rolecall. Loss reporting can therefore exclude genuine same-format escrow without hiding unrelated foreign data. Canonical JSON crosses storage and HTTP through src/entities/runtime-schema.ts, which composes eight strict per-kind decoders. Each adjacent runtime schema uses defineExhaustiveShape<T>() to require exact input and output parity; missing or extra keys, narrowed unions, coercion, any, and never fail typecheck. Unknown same-version keys fail except in declared open bags. Kind-matched profiles are shallow partial bodies whose present fields receive complete validation. Storage, HTTP save, format-corpus verification, and Kit drafts share this ADR-011 boundary.

sections.title: Detection and the registry
sections.summary: src/core/registry.ts holds the in-memory adapter table. Detection runs every adapter, rejects scores at or below 0.5, and selects the single highest-confidence match. Scores encode specificity: a RoleCall card can score 1.0 and outrank the generic SillyTavern reader at 0.9 for the same compatible CCv3 payload. Because character and lorebook adapters share one registry, detectors also enforce a cross-kind firewall. A bare name is insufficient evidence for SillyTavern flat-v1 character data; at least one genuine character signal such as description, personality, scenario, first_mes, or mes_example is required, preventing a name-bearing worldbook from being misclassified.

sections.title: Folders-as-schema (the moddability promise)
sections.summary: src/core/loader.ts is the impure discovery edge. It scans src/formats/*/index.ts with filesystem primitives, dynamically imports each module, and registers its default export. Names beginning with an underscore, including _shared and _template, are ignored. A folder may export one adapter or an array when a format family supplies multiple entity kinds, as SillyTavern and RoleCall do for characters and lorebooks. FormatId is an open string rather than a central enum. Adding a format means copying the template, implementing detection and both canonical directions, and supplying proof; no core registry list or unrelated format file is edited.

sections.title: Bundles: a card plus its lorebook
sections.summary: CCv2 and CCv3 character cards can embed a character_book, but Hoplight models that book as a separate canonical lorebook referenced by the character rather than leaving an opaque nested blob. During import, shared bundle logic extracts the book, creates a CanonicalLorebook, and records its id in knowledgeRefs. During export, the character adapter receives resolved lorebooks through EmitContext and embeds the appropriate target-format representation. The resolved list is authoritative even when empty: removing a link or disabling all linked books clears stale embedded data from the escrowed source twin. convertFile coordinates extraction and re-embedding for ordinary same-kind conversions, keeping bundle behavior format-agnostic at the canonical layer.

sections.title: Semantic content capabilities
sections.summary: Capability folders provide pure operations returning previews, changes, warnings, and platform impact without writing. Kit projects content, studio, transfer, and diagnostics into one catalog. Only pure content gets exact read-or-draft access; deferred apply and writable bridges fail closed until separate safety policy grants an exact name. Search exposes five matches, browse and describe progressively, hidden or duplicate descriptors fail, and deferred exposure resets each user turn while drafts persist. studio_read uses RFC 6901 pointers and paging; oversized values use result_query handles whose store enforces per-entry and aggregate UTF-8 byte caps, a count cap, oldest-first eviction, character paging, and direct-offset recovery beyond capacity. change_query retains proposals; read-effect tools return deterministic observations and are rejected for changing content or claiming changes. docs_query searches indexed metadata and reads authoritative Markdown without arbitrary paths or network. Summaries enter generated indexes only with independent hash-bound APPROVE receipts; source or summary edits invalidate approval. Focused checks validate an author's sidecar; global checks require every approval and current projections. Security classifies only exact catalog-derived names as preview-only; durable apply remains an explicit compareAndSave write with re-read verification.

sections.title: Layering
sections.summary: Dependencies point inward: core has no application dependency, formats depend on core, and CLI or Studio depend on both. The engine does not import UI, database, or framework concerns. Conversion and adapters are proven before a surface wraps them. CLI, the Bun Studio server, and the React client share that engine. Studio uses a primary loopback listener, with optional remote listeners enabled separately.

sections.title: The CLI
sections.summary: src/cli.ts is a thin layer over the shared engine. convert writes a requested or extension-inferred target; inspect reports canonical identity and key fields; label reports detected format and origin; validate checks detection and canonical decoding; formats reads the live registry. ui launches the primary loopback Studio server, while optional remote listeners are enabled separately. Version and help expose release identity and usage.

sections.title: Source of truth
sections.summary: The closing map assigns authority to concrete modules. src/core/canonical.ts owns the wrapper, escrow, and id policy. adapter.ts owns adapter kinds and EmitContext. registry.ts owns detection and lookup, while loader.ts owns filesystem discovery. convert.ts coordinates bundle extraction and re-embedding. src/entities/character/schema.ts and src/entities/lorebook/schema.ts define their canonical supersets. Contributors should change these owners rather than introducing parallel definitions in a UI, command, documentation generator, or format adapter.
